title: Territory — Editor Intro
summary: Editorial opening splash: re-arm the story around the key, the city's invisible systems, and Gunnar's need for one fixed point, then hand directly to his first story-page decision to go up and find north.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B, pre-dawn / early morning
panelPlan: Full-page editorial/title splash with no conventional panel grid. Inside sparse apartment 5B before the household is fully awake: the brass key, contact card and small household map sit on the table in sharp foreground; beyond them, Gunnar is a quiet silhouette at the window looking into the vertical canyon of Brooklyn buildings.

Compose the city as layers of systems Gunnar cannot yet read—street grid below, rooftops above, pipes and wires crossing the frame—while the map and key remain the only things he can presently verify. The eye should naturally travel upward.

The page may imply the roof above through framing, ceiling line, fire escape geometry, or the building's upper silhouette, but do not depict Gunnar already meeting anyone or doing anything that occurs after the next story page.

Integrate the captions as deliberate editorial typography with strong hierarchy and breathing room. Give the single-word caption NORTH substantial visual weight. End with Welcome to TERRITORY. as the issue-title landing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: New York has given them a room, a key, and a list of numbers to call when something goes wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This morning, he wants something better.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Something the city cannot move, rename, regulate, disconnect, or put on a form.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So before breakfast, before the bank, before whatever Carrie has planned for them next—

directionInline.text: This is a non-diegetic opening editorial/title page. It should feel like an invitation into the issue, not a recap. Preserve exact caption text. Make the promise larger than the immediate action while revealing nothing beyond the next story page: Gunnar wants north and is about to go up. Do not show Silas, the phone compass, rooftop metal, a hearth or fire, later neighbors, or any later Issue 3 outcome.

source: Editorial intro/teaser pass developed September 30, 2026.

title: Before Anything Else
summary: The morning after Landfall, Gunnar decides that before the city can become usable he must establish one fixed direction.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment, early morning
panelPlan: Wide: Early morning in 5B. The household is quiet; Gunnar stands at the window studying the light between buildings while Bjorn is awake behind him.
Medium: Gunnar checks the small household map on the table, then looks back toward the window and ceiling as if the room itself is insufficient.
Two-shot: Bjorn watches Gunnar take up the map and head for the door.
Close: Gunnar pauses with his hand on the brass key.
source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.

Medium: He studies the sun angle and building shadows, then makes a small mark on the edge of his paper map.
Wide: The roof door opens behind him; Silas emerges with coffee and stops when he notices Gunnar.
Two-shot: Silas approaches only far enough to be neighborly while Gunnar keeps working.

title: Roof Condition
summary: Carrie is documenting the condition of the placement while Bjorn makes clear that assigned housing is not yet the same thing as trusted shelter.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, bright daytime
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie stands at a stable rooftop work surface with a clipboard and building-condition checklist while Bjorn faces her. The city is bright behind them.
Insert: Carrie checks a condition box and makes a short note; no signature line is emphasized and no other form text is readable.
Medium: Bjorn studies the roofline and building systems rather than the paper.

Wide: In the background, Gunnar and the two male Kin are examining a stack of loose rooftop sheet-metal sections and spare vent pieces that belong to the building; they are not touching installed machinery.
Medium: Gunnar looks toward Bjorn with the expression of someone who has found a second problem.

dialogueInline.text: Condition check. I have to record what was already wrong when you moved in.
You are asking whether the shelter was sound.
I am still testing the shelter.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

directionInline.text: No installed HVAC or active rooftop equipment is being dismantled. The loose metal belongs to the building and has been mistaken for available material.

title: The Second Problem
summary: Carrie discovers that the Kin have identified loose rooftop metal as possible hearth material; their error is ownership, not fire competence.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, daytime
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie turns toward Gunnar, already recognizing from his tone that the paperwork is no longer the only issue.
Wide: First Male Kin and Second Male Kin each hold one loose sheet-metal section from the building's rooftop maintenance stack while Gunnar evaluates the remaining pieces.
Medium: Carrie immediately moves toward them and points at the stack.
Medium: Bjorn watches the work without embarrassment because the material appears unused to him.
Close on Gunnar: He states the purpose plainly.

dialogueInline.text: Why did you say that like we have a second problem?
Why are they carrying roof parts?

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: What Shelter Means
summary: The argument reveals the actual unsettled state: the apartment has walls and heat, but Bjorn does not yet understand or trust the systems that are supposed to carry the household through winter.
settingText: Bushwick apartment roof beside roof-access structure, daytime
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie points from the loose metal to the roof equipment, making clear that the pieces are part of the building even if they were not installed.
Medium: Bjorn answers with the practical standard by which he is judging the placement.
Wide: The Kin hold the metal still, waiting rather than continuing once the dispute is clear.
Two-shot: Carrie explains that the building already has heat through radiators and pipes.
Close on Bjorn: He looks toward the roof access and the unseen apartment below, unconvinced that an invisible system equals a settled household.

dialogueInline.text: The room has walls. It does not yet have winter.
Because the heat comes through pipes.
Boiler downstairs. It heats water. The radiators carry that heat up.
The building. The super. Not you.
That is the part I dislike.
Not controlling what keeps them warm.
We do not control the weather either.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Tactical Difference
summary: Carrie forbids a rooftop hearth while Bjorn explains that winter readiness is a leadership obligation; Gunnar clarifies that they are preparing, not lighting a reckless fire.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, daytime
panelPlan: Three-shot: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar stand beside the returned-to-stillness rooftop material as Carrie states the rule and Bjorn tests whether it describes danger or permission.
Two-shot: Carrie and Bjorn stay on the distinction between impossible and prohibited, neither treating the other as foolish.
Three-shot: Gunnar joins the logic while Bjorn explains that winter readiness is an obligation rather than a preference.
Medium group: Gunnar clarifies that nobody is lighting a fire now; Carrie redirects the future-planning impulse toward a solution that does not consume building property.
Wide: The city and open roof surround the final practical question: what happens if the building heat fails?

dialogueInline.text: You cannot build a hearth on a Brooklyn roof.
Because the roof is shared, the surface can burn, smoke travels, and the building has rules about fire.
None of those make fire impossible.
I didn't say impossible. I said you cannot do it.
A chieftain does not forbid warmth.
If winter finds my people unready, that failure is mine.
Nobody is asking you to let them freeze.
We are not making fire now.
Then correct it without taking apart the building.
You tell me. We call the super. If he doesn't fix it, we escalate.
Many people between us and warmth.
That is why he wants the hearth.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: The Observer
summary: Silas, already known to Gunnar but not yet trusted by the household, appears with his phone after hearing rooftop metal; his concern is nosy but reasonable rather than hostile.
settingText: Bushwick apartment roof and adjacent fire-escape landing, daytime
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie notices movement beyond the immediate group.
Wide: Silas stands on an adjacent fire-escape landing or roof-access edge with his phone raised, documenting the unusual rooftop activity from a respectful distance.
Close on Bjorn: His attention locks onto Silas immediately.
Medium on Carrie: She recognizes him and is more irritated than alarmed.
Medium on Silas: Caught, he lowers the phone slightly rather than pretending he was not watching.
Two-shot Carrie/Bjorn with Silas visible behind them.

dialogueInline.text: I heard metal. I thought somebody was stripping the roof.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

directionInline.text: Silas is curious, wary and intrusive, not smug or malicious. He has a plausible reason to document unfamiliar rooftop activity.

title: No Spears
summary: Bjorn reads observation as possible reporting; Carrie forbids violence, Gunnar names the real risk of losing housing, and Silas makes clear he has not reported them.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, daytime
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn keeps his attention on Silas, treating the phone as a possible line to authority.
Medium: Carrie steps into Bjorn's eyeline with one hand raised, stopping the thought before it becomes action.
Medium: Gunnar looks from Silas to the building roof and states the actual consequence.
Medium on Silas: He lowers the phone completely and says he has not contacted anyone.
Wide: First Male Kin and Second Male Kin begin returning the loose metal to the maintenance stack exactly where it came from.
Two-shot: Carrie takes the unsigned housing form back from Bjorn; neither of them pretends the larger shelter question is settled.

dialogueInline.text: If he carries word to the guards, we lose the room.
Good. And they're putting it back.
If there is a real heat problem, you tell me. I handle the landlord. That's my part.
I accept the room. Not yet the winter.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

title: Nothing From the Building
summary: The Vikings restore every building-owned piece; Silas helps identify where one loose section belongs, and Gunnar and Bjorn derive the correct next rule: any hearth solution must be exterior, contained, and made from material that is actually theirs.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: First Male Kin and Second Male Kin return the loose sheet-metal pieces to the building's maintenance stack while Gunnar checks the arrangement.
Medium: Silas points to the original position of one section from several feet away.
Two-shot: Gunnar verifies the placement with him rather than dismissing the help.
Wide: With the roof restored, Silas leaves toward the fire escape while the Kin carry no building material away.
Medium: Gunnar and Bjorn look across a clear noncombustible area of roof and then up to the open sky.
Final two-shot: The solution has changed from taking material to designing something self-contained that belongs to them.

dialogueInline.text: The sky still solves the smoke.
Then we build with something that is ours.

source: Territory rooftop/hearth revision developed from recovered historical hearth-building and Silas-observer artwork; revised to current character logic and continuity.

directionInline.text: End with no building-owned material removed or damaged. This page must flow directly into P14's later purpose-built contained rooftop stove/fire pit.

panelPlan: Wide: A small contained metal-and-stone rooftop stove/fire pit sits on a stable noncombustible base well clear of surrounding materials; a water bucket and fitted cover are within reach.
Medium: Gunnar checks the wind while Bjorn inspects the base and clearance one final time.
Insert: Gunnar touches the water bucket, confirming it is full.
Medium: Only after the checks are complete does Bjorn light the prepared fuel.
Wide: A modest controlled flame establishes itself; neither man looks surprised by fire.

Medium: Bjorn tends the fire quietly while Gunnar keeps watching the city. On-page Gunnar observation caption, exactly: "I have decided it is not unpleasant."

dialogueInline.text: I need your mark that the building's metal went back and I explained the fire boundary.

title: Neon and Noise
summary: Carrie crosses a small professional boundary by feeding the fire herself; Bjorn completes the already-established witnessed-mark procedure, and the issue ends with the household secure beneath a city they are beginning to know.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof at night
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie waits beside the fire while Bjorn holds his hand over the familiar black ink pad; the spring night is cool enough that she edges closer to the warmth without the rooftop becoming cozy or romanticized.
Insert: Without comment, Carrie picks up one prepared piece of wood and places it carefully into the contained fire.
Close: Bjorn notices the action, then inks his thumb and presses the witnessed mark onto the roof follow-up form.
Medium: Carrie takes the completed paper back immediately, as if paperwork fully explains why she is still there.
Wide: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar remain by the small contained fire for one quiet beat. Bushwick glows and moves around them: windows, traffic, distant music, damp roofs, ordinary spring night.
Final wide: The three are small against the neighborhood, the fire controlled and the city active beyond them.

dialogueInline.text: The perimeter is held by neon and noise, but we are secure.

source: Issue 3 — Territory insertion developed from recovered Finding North / Hearth / fire-escape / Neon and Noise material and locked September 27, 2026 development decisions.
